AC-3 The manifest set contains every object the contract's section 5 names, and each satisfies the construction rules: no root, no fixed UID, no hostPath, no privileged, no host networking, resource requests and limits set, readOnlyRootFilesystem true with each declared writable path supplied as a mount.

AC-9 No credential value is present in any tracked file; the repository privacy gate reports zero findings.

baseline.authority: docs/design/UI2_0_B1_01C_CONTAINER_IMAGE_AND_KUBERNETES_DEPLOYMENT_CONTRACT.md (FROZEN, 2026-09-12) is the implementation authority for this movement: it is the successor contract UI2_0_B1_01A section 6 required, and it decides the image, the arbitrary-UID filesystem model, the build path, the manifest set, the database and empty first state, the secret path, and portability. This movement implements that contract and decides nothing the contract left open.
baseline.prior_attempt: A first attempt at this movement was killed by the orchestrator's default per-movement budget after 22 turns, with the Containerfile, the manifest directory and the manifest rule test written but not committed. Nothing about the scope was found impossible. This dispatch raises the budget and corrects a defective validation step in the previous packet, which ran pytest against the whole test directory instead of the movement's own test file and failed on unrelated collection errors. Neither correction changes what is being built.
baseline.required_first_state: docs/design/PO_DECISION_RECORD_2026_09_12.md (FROZEN) section 4: a clean, empty database, the UI and its menus visible, nothing pre-populated.
baseline.runtime: docs/design/PO_DECISION_RECORD_2026_09_12B_LOCAL_KUBERNETES.md (FROZEN): plain Kubernetes driven with kubectl, one OCI image carried unchanged across three stages, no host container tool in any path, and the image built inside the cluster because the host carries no JDK and no build daemon.
baseline.sequencing: This is the first movement the frozen contract authorizes. The removal of the superseded Line 1 equipment follows it, not precedes it, because a test currently enforces a security invariant against that equipment's own files.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law
The contract is the authority. Where it states a rule, implement that rule; where it records UNKNOWN, report what you observed rather than deciding.
Both base images are referenced by digest, never by a floating tag.
No step may require a host JDK, a host build daemon or any host container tool. If a step appears to need one, stop and report it rather than introducing one.
The database starts empty. Do not seed, and do not add a fixture, demo row or sample device anywhere.
No credential value in any tracked file. The operator document says how the credential is supplied; the repository never contains one.
Bind to this machine only. The deployment is not exposed beyond it.
Do not claim a startup you did not execute. If the stack cannot be brought up in this environment, say so plainly and report the exact failure output.
Publish SESSION_CLOSE with scripts/local_relay.py append using --report pointing at a JSON file you wrote first. Do not pass report JSON inline on the command line.
Do not merge to main. Commit on the lane and publish SESSION_CLOSE.
Commit early and commit often on the lane. A movement that ends with uncommitted work loses it; the previous attempt lost a Containerfile, a manifest set and a test that way.
risks: Reporting a startup that was never executed, which is the failure mode the contract's own acceptance checks exist to prevent.
Introducing a host toolchain dependency because it is the quickest way to get a build working.
Pinning a base image by tag instead of digest, so what was proved can change without a tracked file changing.
Writing a credential into a manifest, an environment file or the operator document.
Deciding an UNKNOWN because a plausible value makes the stack come up.
Touching the superseded Line 1 equipment and breaking the test that enforces a security invariant against it.

unresolved_risks: CONTRADICTION C-1, needs a Product Owner or contract-level decision. B1-1c SEC-4 requires the credential to reach the service as secretKeyRef environment entries. The service does not read a credential from the environment at all: DatabaseConfiguration and FlywayMigrationRunner read four secret files and fail closed on a missing, unreadable or empty one, which is the C1 section 6 rule that B1-1c section 1 names as an authority above itself. Implementing SEC-4 literally would put credential values into the container environment for a code path that never reads them, which is worse for SEC-5 and would not start the service. The higher authority was implemented and the contradiction is reported rather than reconciled: the Secret is mounted as four files and the environment carries their paths, never their values, while the database workload, which does take environment configuration, uses secretKeyRef so the section 11 check 13 grep is also satisfied. Every other clause of section 7 holds unchanged.

CONTRADICTION C-2, needs a contract-level clarification. Section 3.1 mandates the UBI9 OpenJDK 21 family and pins it by digest; that family ships /usr/bin/python3 and /usr/bin/python3.9 at the pinned runtime digest, together with OS-owned .py files under /usr/share/crypto-policies. Section 3.5 states the image contains no Python interpreter and no Python source. Both cannot hold for this base family. Nothing was decided: the build introduces no Python and invokes none, and the setuid and setgid set of the built image is byte-identical to the base, so the build introduced none of those either. Either section 3.5's absence rules bind only what the build adds, or section 3.1's family choice needs an amendment.

U-1 still UNKNOWN. Observed: the packaging task consumes no frontend build output. :service:bootJar ran 15 tasks, none a frontend task, and the builder carries no Node. The static assets the service serves are committed under ui2/service/src/main/resources/static/ and are packaged from there as ordinary resources. What was observed is consistent with the builder carrying no Node; the clause's own evidence is the declared inputs of the packaging task.

U-2 still UNKNOWN. Observed: the check the contract names was run. Under uid 1000860007 there is no passwd entry, and the service started, migrated, served and reached readiness. Spring logged the start under the image's own account name rather than the running uid, which is a lookup that did not resolve and was not load-bearing. The image sets user.home explicitly so the JVM need not resolve one.

U-3 still UNKNOWN. Observed: Gradle egress exists from inside the builder, which downloaded its distribution from services.gradle.org and resolved every declared dependency under the committed lockfiles and verification metadata. Frontend resolution was never exercised because the packaging task does not need it.

U-4 untouched and still UNKNOWN. No corporate platform was contacted and no project-request policy was read. The Namespace manifest carries no quota and no limit-range assumption, so it stays an open precondition rather than a second manifest difference.

U-5 still UNKNOWN. Observed: the check the contract names passed for quay.io/sclorg/postgresql-16-c9s at digest sha256:fbef891e... - a pod admitted with an arbitrary uid and the group left at 0 initialized an empty data directory, created both roles and accepted a connection, with the data directory owned by the running uid and group 0. The community PostgreSQL image was not tested, so the contract's expectation that it fails DB-3 remains an expectation.

U-6 still UNKNOWN, and it is the one gap with an operational consequence. The service exposes /healthz, which returns ok as soon as the web server is up. Migration runs in an ApplicationRunner that executes after the context refresh that starts the web server, so there is a window in which /healthz answers while the schema is not yet complete. MIG-4 holds - a failed migration stops the process - but MIG-3 does not. /healthz is used as the readiness probe because it is what exists; closing U-6 needs a service-side readiness state gated on migration completion, which is outside this movement's scope, and section 11 of the operator document says so plainly rather than papering over it.
U-7 untouched and still UNKNOWN. No corporate directive was read.

U-8 still UNKNOWN. Magnitudes were needed for OS-6 to be satisfiable at all, so they are stated in the manifests as per-stage values under PORT-2: service 200m cpu and 512Mi requested, 1 cpu and 1Gi limited; database 100m cpu and 256Mi requested, 1 cpu and 1Gi limited. There was no load, so these are not an observed run under representative load and are not a decision about U-8.

FIRST-3 observation, reported rather than dismissed. After a first start every product table is empty except audit_redaction_policy, which holds 7 rows. Those rows are created by migration V5 and are the audit redaction policy itself - table name, column name, tier, reason - not product data. The deployment seeds nothing and adds no row. FIRST-3 allows what a migration creates as structure; whether a migration may insert policy rows is B1-2's question, not this movement's.

Build reproducibility hazard, belonging to B1-1a's build definition rather than to the image contract, and changed by nothing here. Three of five build attempts failed. One failed with java.net.UnknownHostException for github.com while the Gradle wrapper was downloading its distribution, which services.gradle.org redirects to. Another failed dependency verification on org.springframework.boot.gradle.plugin-3.3.4.pom resolved from MavenRepo: the plugin marker POM Maven Central serves is not the one the committed verification metadata records, which is the Gradle Plugin Portal's, so when the portal is slow or unreachable Gradle falls back and the build fails closed. That fail-closed behaviour is correct, but it makes BP-5's 'repeatable from the repository alone' conditional on which repository answers first.

Cluster preparation this deployment depends on, documented in the operator procedure and not automated: the local registry addon must be enabled so the in-cluster builder has somewhere to push, the node's container runtime must carry a plain-HTTP host entry for that registry so it can pull what was pushed, and the ingress addon must be enabled for browser reach. None is a host container engine; all three are cluster configuration reached through cluster tooling.

The Ingress sets no ingressClassName and was routed by the local cluster's default class. On a cluster with no default IngressClass it would not be routed. Nothing was added, because an ingressClassName is a per-platform value and PORT-3 forbids introducing a platform-conditional construct before the platform requires one.
